incomplete_fork_gate: mcctrl_process::Context::create_process still copies the original non-null descriptor then returns -95 before publishing a registration. No adopted backend/image/guest success path is enabled.
implemented_slice: MappingFile now holds only a one-shot bootstrap Option<Arc<VmaOwner>>. Successful initial mmap consumes that owner into vm_private_data after all geometry checks. Validation failure leaves the bootstrap owned by the file; repeated mmap rejects.

VmaOwner retains the exact Registration and Mirror. Linux vm_ops.open clones the copied raw Arc without allocation for both split and fork; close consumes one reference and clears vm_private_data. Fault lookup and mirror-clear provenance read this per-VMA owner rather than file-private application ownership.

ForkAdoption compares exact scalar transaction identity and implements Reserved, AdoptedAwaitFirstReturn, FirstReturnPublished, GuestLinkObserved, Linked, AbortRequested, HostRevoked, GuestDestroyed, Released and Quarantined transitions. These helpers are not connected to backend admission in this slice.

Wrong positive first RET, repeated commit, reordered linkage, wrong identity and early ACK reject without the requested transition. Cancellation closes operation admission; outstanding access count blocks HostRevoked; failed revocation blocks guest-destruction permission; release requires separately proven final destruction and exact ACK.

HostRevoked and GuestDestroyed are unsafe proof boundaries with explicit requirements. No production caller currently supplies those proofs. Tests must not be interpreted as real Linux PTE/TLB revocation or a guest VM destructor.

executed_actual_body_vectors: Preserve four previous negative/control tests for inherited child-MM fault rejection and backend worker preparation admission, adapted to the new VMA owner dependency.
Initial mmap validation failure preserves bootstrap and no raw owner; dropping the failed file balances the owner.
One-shot mmap, repeated-mmap rejection, same-MM split, different-MM fork and close balance the raw owner references while the consumed file is neutral.
Successful initial mmap followed by Linux close balances the transferred owner.
Thirteen changed identity fields/variants reject adoption, and eight invalid reserve geometries/identities reject construction.
Duplicate adoption, another PID's positive RET and reordered/duplicate linkage reject before transition.
Negative first or second RET closes access admission.
Event sequence requires admission close, access drainage, host revoke, final guest destruction and ACK; active access, revoke error and early/mismatched ACK are rejected.
Quarantine or missing destruction proof never permits release.
